name: Category Position Review
description: Case-pool variant of Market Share, for Problem Recognition.
formula: Market Share = Company Revenue / Total Market Revenue
business_contexts: a regional grocery chain comparing its own sales to total category sales in its footprint
a telecom carrier comparing its subscriber revenue to the total spent across the industry
a ride-hailing app comparing its bookings to total category spend in its metro
a private-label skincare brand comparing its sales to total category sales at retail
a community bank comparing its deposits to total deposits held across its market
question_patterns: Given the client's own sales and the total spent across the category, what percentage of the category does the client represent?
What portion of the total category does the client currently account for?
Out of every dollar spent in this category, what fraction lands with the client?
Relative to the total category, how big a slice does the client currently hold?
solution_logic: Step 1: Calculate market share = company_revenue / total_market_revenue
key_insight: Market share is always measured against the total market, not against any single competitor — that comparison is what relative market share is for.
common_mistakes: Dividing by a competitor's revenue instead of total market revenue
Confusing market share with relative market share, which compares against the largest rival instead of the whole market
framework_soundbite: Market share is company revenue over the total market — the whole pie, not one rival's slice.
